name: PA-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean anchors the race firmly Republican
Glenn Thompson's incumbency and $1.85M war chest dwarf Ray Bilger's $140K operation
Prediction markets price Thompson at 95% to win
A favorable national Democratic environment trims, but does not close, the gap
model.rationale: The R+19 district, a well-funded incumbent, and markets pricing Thompson at 95% all point the same direction, and no polls or expert ratings suggest anything otherwise. The Democratic-leaning national environment narrows the expected margin modestly but leaves Bilger a heavy underdog.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Thompson or a dramatically stronger national Democratic wave could pull the margin into the low double digits.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Glenn Thompson seeks another term in a north-central Pennsylvania district that leans Republican by nineteen points, a structural advantage that has kept the seat safely in GOP hands. He enters the general election with roughly $830,000 on hand after raising $1.85 million, while Democratic challenger Ray Bilger has raised about $140,000 with minimal outside help on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals: the partisan lean, Thompson's incumbency and financial edge, and prediction markets that price his chances at 95%. The current national environment favors Democrats and would trim the expected margin, but not enough to make the seat competitive. Thompson remains a heavy favorite, with the main uncertainty being how large his winning margin turns out to be.
